name: Barbell Wrist Curl (seated underhand wrist flexion)
camera: Side three-quarter view facing right, showing athlete kneeling beside a flat exercise bench
equipment: Flat bench pad and a compact barbell
positionA: Left panel: Athlete kneels with both forearms resting completely flat along the horizontal bench pad, elbows on the pad, wrists hanging just past the far edge holding a barbell with underhand supinated grip (palms facing upward); wrists are extended downward toward the floor.
positionB: Right panel: EXACT SAME kneeling posture, exact same bench, and EXACT SAME forearm position resting completely flat and horizontal on the bench pad. Athlete only curls his wrists upward toward the ceiling (wrist flexion) raising the barbell 2-3 inches; elbows and forearms MUST NOT lift or move off the bench pad; forearms remain 100% horizontal and glued to the bench pad.
mechanics: Pure wrist flexion. Forearms, elbows, and torso remain completely motionless and flat on the bench pad in both panels.
avoid: NEVER lift elbows or forearms off the bench pad in panel B; do not bend elbows into an arm curl; forearms must stay flat on the bench surface in both panels; no overhand pronated grip, no extra limbs, no text/labels/arrows.

Both poses show the same equipment and geometry
Cuffs and other attachments are visibly connected as specified
